ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All beneficial owners, directors, and authorized signatories must be screened against the KoFIU suspicious transaction report database, the OFAC SDN List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and domestic blacklists published by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit. Enhanced due diligence requires verification of PEP status through public official registries and commercial AML databases, continuous monitoring of transactions for red flags, and annual re-certification of all UBOs. Any positive match requires immediate suspension of incorporation and filing of a Suspicious Transaction Report with KoFIU.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Commercial Registration Information System (i-REG, 인터넷등기소)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All company names must be registered in Hangul (Korean script), with a permissible parallel English trade name for commercial convenience. The name must comply with the four-tier naming doctrine: (1) distinct trade name, (2) business scope descriptor, (3) legal entity suffix such as 'Yuhan Hoesa', and (4) phonetic transliteration of foreign names per National Institute of Korean Language guidelines. The name must not be identical or deceptively similar to existing registrations or trademarks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name application is rejected, the applicant may file a written objection with the Registry Court within 14 days of receipt of the rejection notice. The appeal must state the legal grounds for contesting the rejection, provide a comparative list of previously accepted names used for non-identical distinction, and pay the statutory appeal fee. The Court must issue a decision within 30 days. If the Court upholds the rejection, the applicant may pursue an administrative appeal to the Supreme Court Registry Division or file a new application with a revised name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not accepted by the National Tax Service (NTS) for trading companies because it lacks identifiable business premises and physical records storage. Korean banks also reject virtual addresses under KYC obligations for corporate account opening. A serviced shared office with a physical desk lease and on-site company representative is permissible, but pure mailbox services are disallowed for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) NTS field inspection to verify actual business activity and physical presence; (2) Registry Court ex officio verification if red flags are detected; (3) Bank on-site visits during account opening and periodic reviews. Risk of unannounced physical inspection is Moderate, with higher probability if tax filings are anomalous, third-party complaints arise, or the registered office is a high-density shared address. Maintaining full corporate books, contracts, and a visible company sign substantially reduces risk.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000 of 1962, as amended, Chapter V Limited Company, Articles 543 through 615; Registration of Real Estate and Commercial Registration Matters Act; Local Tax Act for registration tax.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the Local District Court under the Supreme Court of Korea via the I-Deung online registration system; National Tax Service HomeTax for corporate tax and VAT registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Company, together with notarized Articles of Incorporation and capital contribution payment certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act. The incorporator must pay all subscribed contribution units in full into a domestic bank account opened in the name of the incorporator before court registration is filed. The funds remain blocked as a deposit and cannot be withdrawn until the incorporation registration certificate is issued and a corporate operating account is opened. There is no separate government escrow regime; the designated bank acts as depositary and performs source-of-funds verification under Korean anti-money laundering regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: first, that the Company shall be formed as a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, and the Articles of Incorporation presented to this board, incorporating the registered office, capital structure and the authorized business scope of cross-border procurement and distribution of culinary and ceremonial grade organic matcha powder under ISIC 4631, are approved. second, that the total subscribed capital of the Company is set at KRW 10,000,000 represented by 1,000 contribution units of KRW 10,000 each; all units are authorized and deemed subscribed by the founding member, and the representative director is instructed to cause the amount to be paid into a domestic bank deposit account established in the name of the Company's incorporator and to obtain the capital contribution payment certificate required by the Commercial Registration Rules, such amount to remain blocked until registration. third, that the registered office of the Company is adopted and established at [Precise Address, Seoul, Republic of Korea], within the jurisdiction of [Name of Local District Court], and that the representative director is authorized and directed to execute the lease agreement, register the office, open utility accounts, and make all statutory notifications. fourth, that the following banking authorities are granted: the representative director and any one other director, or in case there is no other director, the corporate secretary or the statutory auditor, shall jointly sign all checks, transfer instructions, SWIFT TT payment orders and wire transfer authorizations; any payment above KRW 10,000,000 requires double signatories and compliance with Financial Transactions Reports Act beneficial ownership verification; the banking

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; official electronic portal: Home Tax Service (HTS) at hometax.go.kr; export/customs electronic single window: Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS at unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the domestic Yuhan Hoesa (Korean limited liability company), after incorporation under the Commercial Act, the statutory representative files a business registration application with the competent district tax office of the principal place of business, or submits the same online through the Home Tax Service portal using an authorized digital certificate, within 20 calendar days of business commencement. The application must attach the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, lease agreement or ownership certificate evidencing the Korean business address, passport and proof of authority of the statutory representative, and, if the representative maintains no domestic address, a tax representative appointment notice under the Framework Act on National Taxes. For a foreign non-resident company without a Korean permanent establishment that nevertheless incurs VAT obligations, the procedure is identical except that the non-resident must appoint an approved domestic tax representative, submit the foreign certificate of incorporation, board resolution, power of attorney, certificate of foreign tax residence, and the representative's appointment notice, and the NTS will issue a foreign-entity VAT registration number. The resulting Business Registration Certificate contains the statutory 10-digit Taxpayer Identification Number, which serves concurrently as the corporate income tax TIN and the VAT registration ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not provide a check-the-box election; a Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily classified as a domestic corporation subject to entity-level corporate income tax and separately to VAT. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act apply as compulsory anti-deferral adjustments, not elective classifications.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act, administered by the National Tax Service
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover-based registration threshold exists; any entrepreneur supplying taxable goods or services in Korea must file for VAT registration within 20 calendar days of business commencement regardless of expected revenue. The simplified taxpayer regime for small vendors is a calculation and compliance concession, not a registration exemption, and a corporate wholesaler is in all cases required to maintain full general VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The NTS mandates issuance of an electronic tax invoice (E-Tax Invoice) for all taxable supplies by corporations. E-tax invoice data is transmitted through the Home Tax Service electronic tax invoice channel to the NTS at the time of issue, where it is validated and cross-matched against VAT returns, payment history, cash receipts, and customs export data. There is no separate private-sector pre-clearance stamping requirement; anti-fraud is enforced centrally by NTS in near-real time. Licensed e-invoicing service providers or direct Hometax web submission may be used as the transmission channel, subject to NTS-approved data schema requirements. Paper tax invoices are not permitted as the primary issuance mode for corporate suppliers, and late or non-transmitted e-tax invoice records attract additional tax penalties under the Value-Added Tax Act. For exports, the e-tax invoice must specify the zero rate and cite the Korea Customs Service export declaration reference.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Value-Added Tax Act, exported goods qualify for 0% VAT when a VAT-registered exporter (i) holds a written export sales contract/purchase order, (ii) files and secures an Export Declaration through Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS, (iii) ships the goods to a foreign consignee, evidenced by a Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, and (iv) receives the sale proceeds from abroad through a licensed Korean foreign-exchange bank within the statutory repatriation period. The supply must be identified as an export on the e-tax invoice, with the zero rate applied. Qualifying offshore digital services supplied to non-residents may also be zero-rated but the subject trade is physical matcha powder, so the physical export clearance documentary chain is controlling.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Clearance Confirmation Notification issued electronically by Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS; equivalent to the Bill of Entry)
Original or certified electronic Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill for airfreight) showing shipment from a Korean port to the foreign buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate issued by the Korean settlement bank, evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
Commercial Invoice and complete Packing List, with quantities and unit values agreeing with the export declaration
Export Sales Contract / Purchase Order and the e-tax invoice stating '0% zero-rated export'
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service cross-verify export declarations, e-tax invoices, steamship manifests, bill of lading details, and bank foreign-exchange settlement records. If an export zero-rating claim is unsubstantiated, physically unverified, or fraudulent, the supply is retrospectively reclassified as taxable domestic supply at 10% VAT, input VAT previously credited is clawed back with statutory additional tax, the exporter loses refund entitlement, and the NTS imposes understated tax penalties plus daily overdue interest. Deliberate fabrication or alteration of export documents is additionally punishable under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and the Customs Act, carrying criminal fines, imprisonment, and forfeiture of the goods or proceeds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) is administered by the Bank of Korea.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea maintains a liberalized current-account convertibility regime but applies a comprehensive notification- and approval-based framework for capital-account movements. KRW is not fully convertible offshore; onshore current-account receipts and payments, including trade in goods, can generally be settled without prior BOK license if the transaction is reported through a local foreign exchange bank. Profits and dividends remittance to non-resident shareholders are permitted after tax clearance and submission of audited financial statements, provided the original foreign investment was reported. Capital remittances are subject to documentation and may require a certificate of foreign investment. The surrender requirement for export proceeds is effectively zero as Korea abandoned mandatory conversion; however, exporters must collect proceeds within 180 days and report through FEIS. The main operating hurdle lies in anti-money-laundering documentation for cross-border payments, particularly when the Korean Yuhan Hoesa is owned by a non-resident and funds originate from non-KRW currencies. In summary, Korea is a convertible current-account governed capital-account jurisdiction with intensive Bank of Korea surveillance and no material convertibility restriction for bona fide trade transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, export proceeds for goods must be received within 180 calendar days from the date of export declaration or shipment. Extensions may be granted by the managing foreign exchange bank for realistic delays such as inspection or extended payment terms, but must be registered in FEIS. Mandatory conversion ratio: 0% - South Korea removed the legal surrender requirement; exporters may retain foreign currency in a Foreign Currency Account or convert to KRW at market rates. If the proceeds are not collected within the statutory period, the exporting entity must file an uncollected export proceeds extension or otherwise report the delay to the responsible bank, which triggers heightened trade compliance scrutiny.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore EMI account for a Korean Yuhan Hoesa is legally unviable. The Bank of Korea and Financial Supervisory Service require any entity providing payment or remittance services in Korea to hold an Electronic Financial Business Operator license under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act. Non-Korean digital EMIs are not recognised as equivalent licensed banks; local Korean banks reject the use of offshore EMI virtual accounts for trade settlement, and FEIS reporting cannot be performed through an EMI. Feasibility rating: Low - use only as an ancillary vendor pay-out mechanism, never as a primary clearing rail for matcha procurement or capital transactions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-branch physical appearance is mandatory for at least one authorised representative of the Yuhan Hoesa, typically a statutory domestic director or a delegated attorney with a board resolution and notarised corporate power-of-attorney. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally permitted by major Korean commercial banks for a foreign-owned Korean LLC. A hybrid appointment may be accepted where the physical representative appears in person with an apostilled POA and the non-resident ultimate beneficial owners complete a video KYC interview with enhanced documentary review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner opacity or non-resident shareholder in a jurisdiction with elevated sanctions exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO declaration form, complete shareholder registry, passport and proof of address for each material shareholder, board resolution confirming the ownership chain, sanctions screening reports from UN, EU, OFAC and Korean FSC consolidated lists, and clean-source-of-wealth evidence such as audited financials or bank statements for the remitting entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags including unit price or invoice mismatch against organic matcha market benchmarks
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original sales contract, commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or air waybill, cargo insurance, third-party inspection certificate, phytosanitary certificate, and the relevant Korea Customs Service import or export declaration showing aligned description, quantity, unit price and shipment date.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a non-resident shareholder without clear legal basis for creating equity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Investment Report certificate issued by the Korean foreign exchange bank, notarised capital increase board resolution, subscription agreement, SWIFT MT103 remittance confirmation, and a certificate of foreign investment issued by the bank after the KRW or USD credit is verified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payments or payments from bank accounts not matching the name of the contractual supplier or investor
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written assignment or novation agreement, confirmed purchase contract, bank audit letter from the remitter's financial institution, FEIS reporting numbers from prior related transactions, and a KYC indemnity undertaking supported by the issuing bank's compliance officer approval.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder capital should be routed via a direct SWIFT MT103 transfer from the non-resident shareholder's account to the Yuhan Hoesa's designated foreign currency account at a tier-1 Korean bank. The remittance must clearly reference the Foreign Investment Report and be annotated with the FEIS purpose code for foreign direct investment or equity acquisition. The Korean bank must submit the required Foreign Exchange Transactions report to FEIS within the mandatory timeframe. Capital verification is completed through the bank's foreign investment confirmation notice, credited wire statement, issuance of shares, and registration of the capital increase in the Korean registry.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Organic matcha powder import settlements should be executed through SWIFT MT103 direct credit transfers for spot payment terms, or through import L/C at sight and documentary collection (D/P or D/A) where deferred payment terms apply. Each outflow must be linked to an underlying customs import declaration and submitted to FEIS under the general import purpose code. The appointed tier-1 Korean bank's trade desk should manage the swift message field formatting to include the import declaration number, purchase contract reference, and complete beneficiary bank details.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Tax Return and Financial Statements Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, via HomeTax System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of the year immediately following the fiscal year end; for a calendar-year-end entity, March 31 is the hard deadline; a one-month extension to April 30 is available only if the financial statements have been audited by a certified CPA under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, Etc.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 20% of the under-reported tax for non-filing and 10% for late filing within one month; daily overdue interest of approximately 0.022% (8.03% per annum) accrues on unpaid amounts. Persistent non-filing for three consecutive years may lead to administrative closure of the business registration file by the tax office; Korean courts do not conduct automatic strike-off, but the competent district court may order judicial dissolution on an interested party application if the company has remained inactive for five years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Local Government tax office for the registered head office (Metropolitan City/Province and Si/Gun/Gu)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the corporate tax return deadline: March 31 following the fiscal year end, with matching extension if the corporate tax return is extended; the surcharge is 10% of the final corporate income tax amount.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers 20% additional tax on the unpaid local income tax and overdue interest of 0.025% per day under the Local Tax Act; prolonged non-payment results in asset attachment, bank account seizure, and restriction on issuing local tax payment certificates required for banking and government contracts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Members and Approval of Annual Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing required; signed minutes and complete financial statements must be retained at the registered head office and made available to the district court, the tax office, or foreign exchange authorities on request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be held within three months after the close of each fiscal year; a calendar-year-end entity must hold the meeting and pass the resolution by March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual members meeting is punishable by a criminal fine up to KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 3,800) under Article 635 of the Korean Commercial Act; approved financial statements, member registers, and minute books must be preserved for at least ten years, and loss of those records may lead to a fine and adverse inference in civil or tax disputes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report Submission to Financial Supervisory Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART public disclosure system, under the Securities and Futures Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the fiscal year end for companies subject to statutory external audit; for a calendar-year-end company the audited financial statements and audit report must be submitted by April 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the audit report may result in a penalty up to KRW 20,000,000 (approximately USD 15,000) under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, Etc.; the FSS may also impose corrective orders, daily penalties of 0.05% of the un-filed amount, and refer the case to the prosecution for continued non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Reconciliation and Updating of Members Register and Beneficial Ownership Records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of the competent District Court (for quota transfer registrations); designated Foreign Exchange Bank or Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) for foreign-invested companies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous duty: the members register must be updated immediately upon any transfer of a membership quota; transfer registration must be filed at the District Court within 14 days of the change; for foreign-invested companies, a subsequent foreign investment report must be made within 30 days of the shareholding change. An annual reconciliation should be completed and initialled by the managing member before the annual members meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late commercial registration of a quota transfer attracts a court registration penalty up to KRW 4,000,000 (approximately USD 3,000) and the transfer cannot be asserted against third parties until registered; false entries in the members register may subject the managing member to criminal fines under the Korean Commercial Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 2 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, Etc. (as amended, effective for fiscal years beginning on or after November 1, 2018), a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) is mandatorily subject to an independent certified public accountant external audit if, as of the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year, it meets any one of the following quantitative criteria: (1) total assets of KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,000,000) or more; (2) total assets of KRW 7,000,000,000 or more but less than KRW 12,000,000,000, together with annual revenue of KRW 10,000,000,000 or more and total liabilities of KRW 7,000,000,000 or more; (3) it is a listed company; (4) it is a financial company under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act; or (5) it is designated as an audit-target company under Article 4 of the same Act. A foreign-invested company may additionally be required to submit audited financial statements by its bank, trade counterpart, or the foreign exchange authorities even if the statutory thresholds are not met.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for listed companies. For unlisted entities subject to external audit, the company may apply K-IFRS or K-GAAP (Korean General Purpose Accounting Standards) as set out in the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, Etc. Companies below the statutory audit threshold, such as the small organic matcha powder wholesale operation described in this task, are not required to prepare audited IFRS/GAAP packages but must maintain accounting records sufficient for corporate income tax compliance under the Framework Act on National Taxes; audit working papers and financial statements of externally audited companies must be retained for 10 years under Commercial Act Article 33, with a minimum 7-year retention for audit working papers under the External Audit Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no stand-alone beneficial-owner annual filing for a purely domestic Korean LLC. Instead, the managing member must maintain an accurate members register and a complete minute book, and must update the register immediately for any transfer of membership quotas. A quota transfer becomes effective upon the consent of all members unless the articles of incorporation permit consent by a majority, and the resulting change must be filed with the district court commercial registry within 14 days. If the company is foreign-invested, subsequent changes in shareholding or membership ownership must be reported to the designated Foreign Exchange Bank or KOTRA within 30 days of the change. The company should perform an annual reconciliation of the members register against quota transfer deeds, payment records, approved meeting minutes, and any pledge or charge records before the annual members meeting.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 1,500 per year for a standard commercial registered office address and mail handling in Seoul or a major metropolitan area; USD 1,500 - USD 4,000 per year for a full corporate secretarial and registered agent package including compliance calendar management, document preparation, and liaison with Korean authorities.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 15,000 per year for a small wholesale import and distribution LLC below the mandatory audit threshold but preparing reviewed or agreed-upon-procedure statements for banks; USD 15,000 - USD 50,000 per year for a full statutory external audit under K-GAAP or K-IFRS when the company grows beyond the KRW 12 billion asset threshold or engages in group consolidated reporting.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national marginal rate on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion, plus 10% local income tax surtax (aggregate top effective incremental rate 26.4%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Progressive entity-level rates: KRW 0–200 million at 9%; KRW 200 million–20 billion at 19%; KRW 20–300 billion at 21%; over KRW 300 billion at 24%. No patent box applies to matcha powder wholesale distribution; available reductions include R&D tax credits up to 25% of qualifying expenditure, job-creation and facility-investment credits under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, and foreign-invested enterprise relief in designated Free Economic Zones.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Computation Statement (Corporate Tax Return; primary NTS form filed together with audited financial statements, tax-adjustment schedules, foreign-investment report schedules, and international related-party transaction disclosure forms) submitted electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax system at www.hometax.go.kr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return; quarterly/semi-annual interim advance tax payments for fiscal years exceeding six months.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year taxpayer the statutory deadline is 31 March. Interim tax payments are due within 2 months after the end of the first six months of the fiscal year. Withholding tax remittance and DTA relief applications are payment-date controlled.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business identification: trade name, business registration number, representative director, Korean address, industry code (ISIC 4631 / NAICS 424490), fiscal year, and tax office jurisdiction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Yuhan Hoesa incorporated in Korea is a Korean tax resident and is taxed on worldwide income. Enter the Korean tax identification number and attach the foreign-investment schedule disclosing each non-resident shareholder. The non-resident shareholders themselves are not taxed in this return; their dividends are taxed by separate withholding procedures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales/turnover: total revenue from wholesale distribution of organic matcha powder, including domestic and export sales, reconciled to the K-IFRS or Korean GAAP income statement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all Korean-source revenue and any export revenue booked by the Korean entity. If the foreign parent purchases matcha from Japan or China and resells to the Korean entity, the invoice must reflect actual custody transfer, shipping terms, and insurance. Under-invoiced or over-invoiced entries are an immediate TP audit trigger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold and inventory valuation: procurement from Japanese/Chinese matcha producers, inbound freight, customs duties, inspection, quality control, and inventory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For cross-border procurement from related suppliers, apply the arm’s length standard and file the international related-party transaction schedule. Unsubstantiated COGS, fake supplier invoices, or inventory valuation differences will be disallowed and reclassified as constructive dividends or director remuneration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit and ordinary income: sales revenue less cost of goods sold and operating expenses, before Korean tax-book adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean distributor must earn an arm’s length distribution margin. If the entity consistently reports a loss or near-zero profit while the foreign affiliate earns high margins, the NTS may apply TNMM and adjust the Korean taxable income upward. Maintain gross margin benchmarks for the Korean wholesale food sector.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-book reconciliation: add-back of non-deductible expenses, deduct non-taxable income, depreciation adjustments, entertainment expense limits, and other temporary differences bridging financial net profit to tax-base profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Notional royalties or management fees paid to the foreign parent without economic substance are non-deductible. Interest incurred on loans from non-resident controlling shareholders may be limited under thin-capitalization rules. All adjustments must be supported by tax invoices, contracts, board minutes, and bank statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before loss carryforward: the adjusted tax base after all statutory additions and subtractions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign corporation with a Korean permanent establishment, only income attributable to the Korean PE is taxable. For the Korean-resident Yuhan Hoesa, worldwide income is taxable. Disclose every related-party financing, procurement, and distribution transaction in the attached international transaction schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward offset: current-year taxable income reduced by previously recognized Korean corporate tax net operating losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses may be carried forward 10 years under current Korean law. A merger, demerger, or change in business purpose without NTS tax continuity approval forfeits the loss carryforward. Non-resident shareholders cannot use the Korean entity’s losses to offset their home-country income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income subject to progressive national corporate income tax rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate the tax base in KRW and apply the statutory rate brackets. If the entity has treaty-protected Korean-source income, it must be excluded only through an approved DTA application; do not zero out income on the basis of a free-zone or foreign shareholder arrangement without statutory authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross national corporate income tax: the tentative tax computed at 9%, 19%, 21%, and 24% progressive brackets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This line contains national CIT only. The local income tax surtax of 10% is declared separately. Foreign tax credits for withholding taxes paid abroad on foreign-source income are calculated after gross tax, not as a deduction in this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: R&D expenditure credits, job-creation credits, facility-investment credits, foreign-investment tax credits, and any other non-refundable credits under Korean special taxation law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned matcha distributor may claim R&D/job credits only if Korean employees perform qualifying activities inside Korea and the payroll, contracts, and time records are retained. Credits cannot be claimed on an overseas parent’s intangible development or brand expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local income tax surtax: 10% of the national corporate income tax payable after credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean entity remains subject to local income tax even if all shareholders are non-resident. Treaty reductions apply to national income tax only to the extent permitted, and the local surtax follows the national tax refund or assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepayments and interim taxes: deduction of semi-annual interim tax payments, withholding credits, and estimated payments already made during the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile all HS codes and bank wires used for customs and payments in order to match interim payment records. If interest or royalty income received from Korean sources was subject to 22% withholding, attach the withholding certificate and claim it as a credit against final CIT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax payable or refundable: national tax plus local surtax less prepayments and credits, including penalty taxes and interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be made by the statutory deadline to avoid late-payment surcharges. A subsequent dividend distribution to foreign shareholders is not deductible here and is subject to separate dividend withholding tax; any attempt to characterize dividends as interest or service fees is a criminal red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International related-party transactions and TP disclosure: schedules listing cross-border transactions with related parties, transfer-pricing methods, Local File, Master File, and country-by-country reporting declarations where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose every cross-border payment for matcha purchase, royalty, interest, service, or management fee. Annual related-party transactions of KRW 5 billion or more trigger mandatory disclosure; annual revenue over KRW 100 billion plus related-party transactions over KRW 10 billion trigger Local File and Master File submission. Inconsistent or missing TP filings are fatal in an audit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file by the statutory deadline triggers unfaithful-return additional tax under Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-2, generally 10% of understated tax for faithful but inaccurate returns, 20% for failure to file, and up to 40% for fraudulent or false returns, plus late-payment surcharge interest accruing daily until full payment. Intentional concealment or evasion is referred to prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to three times the evaded tax in aggravated cases. For TP documentation failures, the NTS may impose penalty fines up to KRW 30 million and adjust taxable income using discretionary methods.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax plus 10% local income tax surtax, producing an aggregate statutory dividend withholding rate of 22%; applicable to dividends paid by the Korean entity to non-resident shareholders. Tax treaties may reduce the rate to 5%–15% depending on the residence jurisdiction and shareholding level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a bilateral DTA: (1) obtain an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the shareholder’s tax authority clearly identifying the owner and the covered tax year; (2) complete the Korean non-resident tax treaty relief application form and file it through HomeTax or with the competent district tax office before the dividend/interest/royalty payment date or within the statutory refund claim window; (3) provide a beneficial ownership declaration with supporting economic-substance evidence, including board minutes, employment records, office/warehouse presence, contracts, bank statements, and proof that the recipient is not a conduit; (4) ensure the principal purpose of the arrangement is not treaty shopping; if the Korean withholding agent has already withheld at the statutory rate, the non-resident may file for a refund with the National Tax Service.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding rates on cross-border interest and royalties are 20% national tax plus 10% local surtax, aggregate 22%. DTA rates commonly reduce interest and royalty withholding to 10%–15%, with certain government/central-bank interest exemptions. For a matcha distribution business, avoid dressing layer profits as royalties; trade intangibles and brand fees must reflect genuine ownership, transfer-pricing analysis, and Korean cost-bearing substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File preparation is triggered when annual revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion. Annual disclosure of international related-party transactions is required on the corporate tax return when the aggregate transaction amount with overseas related parties is KRW 5 billion or more.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not impose a separate UAE-style Economic Substance Return, but substance is legally required under the substance-over-form principle, Controlled Foreign Company rules, the International Tax Adjustment Act, and the OECD Principal Purpose Test. The Korean matcha distributor must demonstrate Core Income-Generating Activities in Korea, including procurement negotiation, inventory risk, quality control, local sales contracts, invoicing, logistics, and distribution decision-making. A passive Korean entity with no employees, no office, and no business risk used to invoice related-party matcha transactions will be pierced, treated as a PE of the foreign principal, or denied treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Intentional Corporate Tax Evasion / False Corporate Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying directors' personal matcha consumption and travel expenses through the company, omitting cash or overseas rebate income from matcha suppliers, fabricating purchase invoices from fictitious organic matcha producers, or reporting inflated cost of goods sold to reduce the Korean corporate income tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Articles 3(1) and 3(2): imprisonment with labor for up to 2 years or a fine not exceeding twice the evaded tax; where the evaded tax exceeds KRW 500 million, imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine up to three times the evaded tax. The NTS also imposes unfaithful-return additional tax up to 40% under Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-2 and disallows the false deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A court may pierce the corporate veil where the Yuhan Hoesa is a mere alter ego or abused as a sham. Directors are jointly and severally liable to the tax authority and injured parties under Commercial Act Article 401 for intentional or gross-negligent acts; the NTS may impose secondary liability on the director’s personal assets under Framework Act Article 23, issue an overseas departure restriction/blacklist, and seek criminal imprisonment personally against the director, which is not dischargeable by corporate liquidation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Documentation Default / Shell Margin Strip
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling organic matcha powder to a related Singapore, Hong Kong, or Chinese distributor below the arm’s length range; shifting Korean procurement and distribution profit to a zero-tax or low-tax affiliate; failing to prepare Local File and Master File after the statutory thresholds are exceeded; submitting a TP study with no comparability analysis, no Korean substance, and no explanation of inventory risk or freight ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: International Tax Adjustment Act Articles 4 and 5 authorize the NTS to re-compute Korean taxable income at the arm’s length price; Article 13 and Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-2 apply understatement penalties up to 20%–40% of the adjusted tax; failure to submit TP documentation may be fined up to KRW 30 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve a fictive transfer price or false TP policy may be treated as joint tortfeasors; Commercial Act Article 401 imposes direct personal liability for damages caused to the Korean company and the National Tax Service. Aggravated TP fraud accompanied by false invoices is prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, and directors face asset seizure, travel bans, and imprisonment for intentional evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding / DTA Relief Abuse and Shell Beneficial Ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, or royalties to a foreign parent or a Hong Kong/BVI conduit without withholding the 22% aggregate WHT; using a shell holding company with no office, employees, or economic activity solely to claim a tax treaty rate; obtaining a Tax Residency Certificate for the wrong period or from a jurisdiction with no substantive tax residence tests; or re-characterizing dividends as deductible management fees to shift profits offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS will deny treaty benefits under the OECD Principal Purpose Test reflected in Korean case law and the International Tax Adjustment Act, assess the full 22% statutory withholding, and impose withholding penalty additional tax under Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-4 (up to 50% of the unwithheld amount) with statutory interest. A false TRC or fraudulent withholding omission triggers criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Articles 3(1) and 3(2).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director acting as withholding agent is personally liable for the uncollected withholding tax and surcharges if he knowingly caused the omission; a Korean court may pierce the corporate veil and hold the director jointly and severally liable. Measures include NTS blacklisting with an overseas departure ban, seizure of personal bank accounts and real estate, joint and several civil restitution to the tax authority, and criminal imprisonment up to 5 years for aggravated tax evasion through sham shareholders and treaty abuse.
